notes.text: Nathan MacKinnon is out (lower-body injury) and missed their last game. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Brock Nelson has taken his spot beside Artturi Lehkonen and Martin Nečas.
Cale Makar is out (lower-body injury) and missed their last game. He is a top-pair defenseman. Sam Malinski has taken his spot beside Devon Toews.
Alex Gagne was added to the roster on Nov 10.
Zachary L'Heureux is no longer killing penalties: 3% of the team’s shorthanded time in 3 games, down from 36% with his old team last season.

The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 30% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the third-lowest in the league (a typical team: 41%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.
Nate Schmidt is on injured reserve and has missed the last 5 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters.
John Marino is on injured reserve (upper-body injury) and has missed the last 13 games. He is a top-pair defenseman.
Nick Schmaltz is on injured reserve (lower body injury) and has missed the last 3 games. He is a top-six forward.
Dylan Guenther is on injured reserve (upper-body injury) and has missed the last 4 games. He is a top-six forward. Clayton Keller has taken his spot beside Vincent Trocheck and Logan Cooley.
Logan Cooley returned in their last game after missing 3 games. Their recent numbers were built mostly without him.

stakes: The Mammoth go in tied for fifth in the Central with 23 points, 4 points behind the Avalanche, tied for third.

UTA.head: The Mammoth have a lot going for them
UTA.body: The two have been about even at out-chancing opponents lately. Utah will be without Schmidt, but Colorado will be without MacKinnon, and the Mammoth have home-ice advantage. The Avalanche can make it interesting if they keep dangerous shots away.

COL.head: A tough matchup for the Avalanche
COL.body: The two have been about even at out-chancing opponents lately. Colorado will be without MacKinnon, while Utah has home-ice advantage. Utah will be without Schmidt, though. The Avalanche can pull it off if they keep dangerous shots away.

story.head: Something has to change for the Mammoth
paras: The Mammoth are winless in six (0-3-3), while the Avalanche (12-6-3) beat Montréal 4-1 on Saturday. This is a Central Division matchup, with the Avs third (tied for tenth in the NHL) and the Mammoth fifth (tied for 16th).

The Avalanche’s record (.643) is about what their chances are worth. The Mammoth have played better than their record (.523) says: their chances are worth about .703, and their goaltending has held them back.

The Avalanche do a lot of their shooting from distance (lowest), play the league’s fastest games (1st) and get their defensemen shooting (2nd). Colorado has scored 4.05 goals a game, the second most in the league. On the other side, the Mammoth rarely get pinned in their own end (1st) and let the point shots come and guard the net (1st). They also get more of their shots from in close than almost anyone (3rd), so the Mammoth get in close, but the Avalanche mostly shoot from distance. Something has to give when the Avalanche’s shooting runs into the Mammoth’s defense.

Martin Nečas (10 G / 14 A / 24 P in 21 GP) leads the Avalanche in scoring, and Artturi Lehkonen (15 G / 6 A / 21 P in 21 GP) has a team-high 15 goals, fifth in the NHL. For the Mammoth, Clayton Keller (5 G / 23 A / 28 P in 22 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Logan Cooley (11 G / 11 A / 22 P in 19 GP) has a team-high eleven goals.
Mackenzie Blackwood (11-3-1 / .905 SV% in 15 GS) is expected to go for Colorado. Sebastian Cossa (4-2-1 / .864 SV% in 7 GS) has had a rough start to the season for Utah, but is expected to start.

items.text: The Avalanche are newly without Nathan MacKinnon and Cale Makar. Taking into account how much value each of these missing players usually adds, no team is missing more right now.

The Mammoth are newly without Nick Schmaltz, and have been without Nate Schmidt, John Marino and Dylan Guenther for several games. Taking into account how much value each of these missing players usually adds, only the Avalanche and the Senators are missing more right now.
Anders Lee has four goals in six games against Colorado since 2023-24, most of them with the Islanders.
Artturi Lehkonen has 15 goals on chances worth about 7.9 goals, well above what his finishing usually turns chances into. Runs like that tend to cool off.
